title: Standardize verification tags & deprecation policy for published performance profiles
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Currently, published Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) are created through a mix of automated benchmarks and ad-hoc manual edits. There is no standard tagging scheme, no clear deprecation lifecycle, and limited telemetry hooks to detect regressions after publish. This causes customer confusion when a model variant's measured latency slips or when multiple similarly named profiles exist for the same model/version.
background: We onboard many open models and variants; each publishes a performance profile used by routing, catalog UI, and billing heuristics. As models evolve (weights, quantization, kernel changes), profiles need well-defined version pinning, deprecation notices, and a signal-driven revalidation flow. PMs currently depend on ENG to add ad-hoc notes in the catalog, and console UX teams need deterministic flags to show 'stale' or 'verified'.
goal: Deliver a reproducible policy and automation that:
goals_list: Define a canonical set of verification tags (e.g., verified-stable, verified-experiment, unverified) and metadata fields for each published profile
Implement a time- and event-based deprecation lifecycle for profiles with automated notifications and UI flags
Add telemetry and periodic revalidation jobs that surface regressions (latency/throughput/cost) and auto-open follow-up issues when thresholds are crossed
Provide a lightweight publish API and CLI for Ops/Onboarding to publish profiles with required metadata and provenance links
acceptance_criteria: Catalog entries support the new verification tags and required metadata fields (measurement window, hardware, quantization, dataset used, measurement date)
Console shows a clear 'verification state' and 'last validated' timestamp for each profile
Automated daily revalidation job runs on a sampled workload and opens ENG issues when deviation > 10% latency or > 15% cost increase compared to published profile
Publish API exists with authentication and writes an immutable provenance link to the model's onboarding artifact
A deprecation workflow exists: soft-deprecate (UI flag + 60d), hard-deprecate (remove default routing + 90d) with email/webhook notifications to profile owners
milestones: M1: Tagging spec + schema (2026-03-05) - spec doc and JSON schema for profiles
M2: Publish API & CLI prototype (2026-03-19) - minimal publish path for Ops
M3: Console UI flags & catalog filters (2026-03-31) - render verification state
M4: Revalidation job & alerting (2026-04-07) - daily checks and ENG issue auto-creation
M5: Deprecation automation + comms templates (2026-04-08) - email/webhook + policy page
out_of_scope: Full-size benchmarking pipeline rewrite (we will rely on existing verified-benchmark-pipeline infra)
Changing the runtime scheduling algorithms themselves
implementation_notes: Use the existing benchmark harness (ENG-4821) as the measurement runner; add a lightweight adapter to emit profile-shaped metrics
Profile schema must include: model_id, model_version, hardware_profile, quantization, seq_len_distribution, measurement_image_hash, profile_tag
Pinning behavior: "pinned_version" metadata field will be respected by routing to avoid auto-fallback to newer model variants unless explicitly opted-in
The publish API should store: publisher, timestamp, provenance_link (Confluence/Drive), raw_benchmark_artifact (s3 path), and verification_tag
risks: False positives: noisy infra or contention could trigger unnecessary deprecations; mitigate with multi-run smoothing and increased sample size
Owner availability: many open-source model owners are external; need clear contact + escalation paths
Backward compatibility: older profiles without the new schema must be surfaced as 'legacy-unverified' until migrated
open_questions: What thresholds should we use for throughput regressions for bursty inference patterns? (ENG input required)
Should we support a 'manual override' on the console allowing product teams to mark a profile as verified despite telemetry alerts?
How long should we retain raw benchmark artifacts for auditability vs storage cost concerns?
